title: Check: control plane failures
description: Five questions on diagnosing the cluster's own components.

questions.prompt: kubectl returns 'connection refused' against the API server. Where do you look first?

options.text: crictl on the control plane node, and the static Pod manifest

questions.explanation: With kubectl dead you fall back to the node: `crictl ps -a`, `crictl logs`, and /etc/kubernetes/manifests.

questions.prompt: etcd is down. What still works?

options.text: Running Pods keep running; no cluster state can be read or written

questions.explanation: The data plane is independent. Everything that needs the API stops.

questions.prompt: New Pods are Pending, existing ones healthy, and `kubectl get nodes` works. Which component?
questions.explanation: A working API rules out etcd and the API server. Pending with no node assignment is the scheduler's signature.

questions.prompt: After a year of neglect kubectl reports a certificate error. What is the likely cause and fix?

options.text: kubeadm certificates expired; renew with kubeadm certs renew
The CA was deleted; reinstall the cluster

questions.explanation: kubeadm certificates last a year. `kubeadm certs check-expiration` tells you before it becomes an outage.

questions.prompt: Write the crictl command that lists containers including exited ones.
questions.explanation: Then `crictl logs <id>` reads a control plane container's output when kubectl cannot.
